title: Deuxième partie : variations sur l'équation des lacets [suite à La "Longue Marche" à travers la théorie de Galois…, pages 293 à 650, dont table des matières] : notes et copies de notes manuscrites (s.d.).

deep.reconstruction:
Context (pp. ~610-630 of 'variations sur l'équation des lacets'): M is a profinite 'arithmetic Teichmüller' group. Roughly, it is the extension of (a variant ~ of) Γ_Q = Gal(Q̄/Q) by the profinite π1 of U_{0,3} = P^1−{0,1,∞}, enlarged by the S_3 of symmetries of {0,1,∞}. M^! and M_0^! are subgroups of it. Its 'sections' over Γ_Q correspond, up to ~, to rational points and tangential base points of U_{0,3}, which is the section-conjecture philosophy.

An order-3 element ρ (lifting z ↦ 1/(1−z)) generates L_ρ ≅ Z/3. The fixed points of ρ are −j and −j², the roots of z²−z+1, with j a primitive cube root of unity; they are defined over Q(j) = Q(√−3). The page studies:
- the centralizer Z_ρ = Cent_M(L_ρ) and its part Z_ρ^! = Z_{ρ,o}^! × μ ≅ Γ'^~_Q × μ, with μ = μ_2 central and Γ'_Q of index 2 in Γ_Q, presumably Gal(Q̄/Q(√−3));
- the group N_ρ^? = μ_{τ'}·Z_ρ^!, where τ' is an involution inverting ρ. It is semi-direct, and τ' does NOT normalize the factor Z_{ρ,o}^!.

The previous page gives an exact sequence 1→μ→N_ρ^?→γ_{ρ,σ}=Γ^~_Q→1, so N_ρ^? is a 'quasi-section of multiplicity 2' of M→Γ^~_Q.

On this page:
- (23) reconstructs M, and the normalizer N_ρ, as contracted products over μ_2 of N_ρ^? with S^{+∧} (resp. with L_ρ). It writes N_ρ ≅ N_ρ^? × L_ρ with L_ρ ≅ Z/3.
- The extension (22) of γ_{ρ,σ} induced in the 'principal section' is said to be split.
- (24) gives a canonical map γ_{ρ,σ} ⇒ N_ρ^?/μ → N_ρ^*/μ. After dividing by μ this is an honest (partial) section attached to the fixed point −j of ρ. The next page names it M(−j) and identifies it with the point −j ∈ U_{0,3}(Q(√−3)), whereas the section in case b) corresponds to the point 1/2, fixed by an involution.

Remark: to be complete one must make explicit how τ (complex conjugation, image τ' in Γ_Q) acts on Z_ρ^! ≅ Γ'^~_Q × μ. This action should be inner conjugation on Γ'^~_Q, twisted by a character Γ'^~_Q → μ = {±1}. Grothendieck bets that this character is ε_2, presumably the quadratic character of Q(i) (with ε_3 that of Q(√−3); the next page uses ker(ε_2ε_3) ↔ Q(√3)). Then Γ^{o~}_Q = Γ^~_Q ∩ Γ'^~_Q would be τ'-invariant. He proposes redoing the study of the extension in the principal section starting from the fixed points of α or β (the order-2 elements), 'probably simpler'.

In modern terms: this is the study of finite (torsion) subgroups of the arithmetic fundamental group of the orbifold [U_{0,3}/S_3]. Up to the central μ_2, this is π1 of the j-line / M_{1,1} over Q. Each torsion subgroup's normalizer gives a Galois section attached to an orbifold (CM) point: j=0 ↔ −j for order 3, j=1728 ↔ {−1, 1/2, 2} for order 2. Galois acts on the stabilizers via quadratic or cyclotomic characters.
errors: Equation labels (23), (24) follow (28)-(30) on the previous page; the numbering is inconsistent, likely a renumbering slip.

N_ρ = N_ρ^? ∧_{μ2} L_ρ ≅ N_ρ^? × L_ρ with L_ρ ≅ Z/3: a contracted product over μ_2 requires μ_2 ⊂ L_ρ, so L_ρ there should be of order 6 (μ_2 × Z/3). Also, since τ' ∈ N_ρ^? inverts ρ, the decomposition cannot be a direct product of groups. At best it is semi-direct, or a bijection of underlying spaces.

The guess that the twisting character is ε_2 is unverified. For the j=0 point of M_{1,1} the automorphism group μ_6 carries the mod-6 cyclotomic action, which is trivial on μ_2. So the relevant character may instead be ε_3 or trivial, depending on normalizations. On the next page Grothendieck himself admits 'je suis en train de déconner', having lost contact with the geometry.

ideas.what: Conjugacy classes of finite (order 3, order 2) subgroups of the arithmetic fundamental group, and their normalizers, yield (partial) Galois sections attached to the fixed points −j and 1/2 of the S_3-action on P^1−{0,1,∞}.
ideas.modern_name: Torsion in arithmetic Teichmüller / GT-type groups; sections at orbifold (CM) points of M_{1,1} or [U_{0,3}/S_3]
ideas.usually_credited_to: Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura (1990s); B. Collas and Collas–Maugeais (2010s) on Galois action on torsion of genus-0 Teichmüller groups
ideas.where_published: Esquisse d'un programme mentions the role of finite-order elements / 'points à automorphismes' of the Teichmüller tower in generators-and-relations for the Galois action; no detailed published form known.

ideas.what: A normalizer that is an extension of Γ_Q by μ_2, i.e. a 'quasi-section of multiplicity 2', which becomes a genuine section after quotient by μ.
ideas.modern_name: Sections of stacky/orbifold fundamental group sequences; μ_2 gerbe (center of SL_2)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard in work on π1 of M_{1,1} (e.g. Nakamura, Hain–Matsumoto)

ideas.what: Galois (complex conjugation) action on the centralizer, described as inner conjugation twisted by a quadratic character ε_2 (field Q(i)), with ε_3 ↔ Q(√−3); the next page uses ker(ε_2ε_3) ↔ Q(√3) for a further partial section M(√3) or M(j).
ideas.modern_name: Galois action on automorphism groups of CM points via cyclotomic/quadratic characters
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical (CM theory); in the anabelian setting, Collas

missed.claim: Grothendieck proposes re-deriving the 'principal section' extension starting from the fixed points of the order-2 elements α, β, rather than from global data. He also predicts that the twisting character on the centralizer of the order-3 torsion is ε_2. This program of reading the Galois action off torsion and its fixed points was later carried out in substance (GT relations from the order-2 and order-3 relations; Collas' work on torsion), but this specific ε_2 prediction is not something I can confirm in the literature.
missed.quote: il y a fort à parier que celles-ci sont justement ε_2 ... il y aurait lieu de reprendre l'étude de l'extension faite dans la section principale en y partant des [points?] de un des α, β associés
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Mostly of historical interest. It shows Grothendieck anticipating the torsion/CM-point approach to the Galois action on π1(M_{0,4}) and M_{1,1}, but the mathematics is now standard.

deep.surprise_reason: This is a working, partly self-admittedly muddled computation (the next page says 'je suis en train de déconner'). It concerns normalizers of order-3 torsion and the sections attached to −j. The idea that torsion and orbifold points give Galois sections and constrain GT is known through Drinfeld/Ihara's relations and the work of Lochak–Schneps, Nakamura and Collas. Nothing here appears to go beyond that literature.
transcription_corrections: 'Z_{ρ_0}^! × μ' in the Remarque should read Z^!_{ρ,o} × μ (index ρ,o as on the previous page).
'(NB τ_Γ n'est [?] par l'élément de Γ_Q ⊂ Γ_Q^~, "conjugaison complexe")' likely reads 'τ_Γ n'est autre que l'image de l'élément ... "conjugaison complexe"'.
The superscript insertion reads roughly 'ou d'une "correction quadratique" des Γ'^~_Q' (uncertain), not 'condition [?]'.
'en y/partant des pôles de un des α, β' probably reads 'en y partant des points [fixes] de un des α, β associés'.
The struck word before (22) is overwritten by a word that may be 'extensions' or 'caténaires'; uncertain.
In (23) the struck symbol before L_ρ is a crossed-out bold Z/L; the underlined term reads L_{-ρ} with '≃ Z/3Z' beneath.
